samples.summary: CLI folder/copy/move tests mock away HttpClient entirely, so the new client methods' URLs and body shapes are never verified
samples.evidence: folders.test.ts:22-33 replaces `HttpClient` with a stub class, so `listFolders`/`createFolder`/`renameFolder`/`moveFolder`/`deleteFolder`/`copyDocument`/`moveDocument` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:311-344) are never executed. The only assertions about the wire (`url`, `body`) come from `printDryRun` calls whose path/body strings are re-built independently inside packages/cli/src/commands/folders.ts and docs.ts. If `moveFolder` sent `{ parent: id }` or hit `/folder/:id`, every test here would still pass while the dry-run preview showed the correct request. packages/cli/test/http-client-paths.test.ts is the existing pattern for exercising the real client against a fetch mock, and none of the new methods were added to it.

samples.summary: No test exercises the new Prisma `folder: { disconnect: true }` / `connect` update against a real database
samples.evidence: documents.controller.spec.ts asserts only that `updateDocument` was called with the object the controller just built (e.g. `data: { folder: { disconnect: true } }`), which is tautological with respect to whether Prisma accepts that shape for the Document.folder relation. The e2e lane has packages/backend/test/folder.e2e-spec.ts covering the *web* routes (`PATCH /documents/:id` with `folderId`), but nothing added here covers `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id` with `folderId: null` or `POST .../copy`, so the persisted move-to-root behaviour — the headline feature — is only asserted against a mock.

samples.summary: `create`'s cross-workspace parent check is asserted only as 'was called', not as 'blocks the create'
samples.evidence: folders.controller.spec.ts:74-79 ('checks a supplied parent belongs to the route workspace') calls the controller with a resolving `assertSameWorkspace` mock and only asserts `toHaveBeenCalledWith('f-9', WS)`. There is no test with a rejecting `assertSameWorkspace` asserting `folderService.create` is not called, so a controller that called the assertion after (or ignored) the create — filing a folder under another workspace's parent — would still pass. The sibling documents spec does have this test ('refuses a folder from another workspace').

samples.summary: The manager gate is never exercised for the move-to-root (`parentId: null` / `folderId: null`) path
samples.evidence: In folders.controller.spec.ts the forbid test uses `parentId: 'f-2'` and the null test uses `req(AUTHOR)` (a manager); documents.controller.spec.ts does the same (`folderId: 'f-1'` for the forbid case, `req(AUTHOR)` for the null case). No test asserts a plain member is refused a move to the workspace root, so a regression that placed the manager check inside the non-null branch — letting any member yank documents/folders out of a folder — would not be caught.

samples.summary: No test asserts the `folders` namespace is wired onto the default program
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/namespaces.test.ts builds its own program and calls `registerFoldersCommand(p)` itself, so it proves nothing about cli.ts. The one test that checks the real default program (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:921 'wires every namespace onto the default program') lists login/logout/status/ctx/docs/sheets/slides/notes/api-keys/schema and was not extended with 'folders'. Deleting the `registerFoldersCommand(program)` line from cli.ts would leave the whole suite green while the command vanished for users.

samples.summary: `copy` has no test for an API-key caller, and none asserting no membership/manager check is required by design
samples.evidence: The copy describe block only covers `req(MEMBER)` (JWT). `copy` passes `Number(req.user.id)` to `documentCopyService.copy` as the new author; for an API key `req.user.id` is the minting user, and nothing asserts that path (contrast the deliberate 'allows a write-scoped API key…' tests written for `update` and for folders). A wrong/NaN author id on the copy would silently produce ownerless duplicates.

samples.summary: New schema aliases (folder.*, doc.copy, doc.move) are added but not covered by the alias-resolution tests
samples.evidence: registry.ts adds aliases `['folder.list', 'folder.create', ...]` and `['doc.copy', 'document.copy', ...]`, but schema.test.ts's 'alias resolution' describe (lines ~183-220) was not extended; the only new assertions are name-presence and safety-class checks. A typo'd alias in the registry would not be caught.

samples.summary: 'lets the workspace owner move any document' asserts only `toHaveBeenCalled()` with no arguments
samples.evidence: documents.controller.spec.ts 'lets the workspace owner move any document' (and the folders analogue 'allows a write-scoped API key to move without a membership check') assert `expect(documentService.updateDocument).toHaveBeenCalled()` / `folderService.update).toHaveBeenCalled()` without checking the payload, so the test would pass even if the owner's move wrote the wrong parent. The neighbouring tests do check arguments, so the gap is contained.
